```{=latex}
\quickfacts{OUTPUT}{Multi-chapter document (HTML / PDF)}{STRUCTURE}{One project, \texttt{chapters:} list decides order}{BEST FOR}{Lecture notes, handbooks, theses}
```

## 1 — Setup

**Install (once per computer):**

- **VS Code** — [code.visualstudio.com](https://code.visualstudio.com) (tick **"Add to PATH"** during setup)
- **Quarto CLI** — [quarto.org/docs/get-started](https://quarto.org/docs/get-started/)
- **Quarto extension** for VS Code — search "Quarto" in the Extensions sidebar

**Create the project:** **File → New File… → Quarto Project → Book Project** → choose your folder. Quarto creates:

- `_quarto.yml` — book title, author, and chapter order
- `index.qmd` — cover / preface page
- `intro.qmd`, `summary.qmd` — example chapters (rename or replace)
- `references.bib` / `references.qmd` — bibliography file and its rendered page

```{=latex}
\begin{spotlight}{Which one do I need?}
Writing something long that's read front-to-back, in order --- lecture notes, a handbook, a thesis --- with an automatic table of contents and Previous/Next navigation? This is it. For loosely-linked standalone pages, see the \textbf{Website} cheatsheet; for one short, printable handout, see the \textbf{Exercise Sheet} cheatsheet.
\end{spotlight}
```

{{< pagebreak >}}

## 2 — Organizing & writing chapters

**Every chapter is a `.qmd` file.** The order they appear in `_quarto.yml` is the order they appear in the book:

```yaml
book:
  title: "My Lecture Notes"
  author: "Your Name"
  chapters:
    - index.qmd
    - intro.qmd
    - summary.qmd
    - references.qmd
```

**Add a chapter:** create the new `.qmd` file, then add its filename to the `chapters:` list.

Each chapter file itself is written exactly like any other Quarto page — `##` headings, code cells, callouts, citations — see the Website cheatsheet for Markdown basics.

::: {.callout-tip}
## Tip
The reader gets a **left sidebar** with all chapters, **Previous / Next** links at the bottom of each page, and a **table of contents** for the current chapter — all generated automatically from the `chapters:` list.
:::

**Preview vs. Render:**

| Command | What it does | Use it when |
|---|---|---|
| `quarto preview` | Opens a live view with sidebar & navigation; updates on save | While you're writing and editing |
| `quarto render` | Builds the final book into `_book` (or `docs/`, if configured) | Before publishing |

{{< pagebreak >}}

## 3 — Publish with GitHub Pages

A rendered book's `_book` folder works exactly like a website's `_site` folder — the steps are identical:

1. In `_quarto.yml`, under `book:`, add `output-dir: docs`
2. Render: `quarto render`
3. Create a **public** repository on [github.com](https://github.com)
4. Upload the whole project folder (including `docs/`) and commit
5. Repo → **Settings → Pages** → Branch `main`, folder `/docs` → **Save**
6. Wait for the green checkmark under **Deployments** — your book is live at
   `https://<username>.github.io/<repo-name>/`

**Updating your book later:** run `quarto render` again, then re-upload the `docs/` folder to GitHub (or `git push` if you're using Git).

```{=latex}
\begin{spotlight}{Good to know}
\begin{itemize}
\item Group chapters into named sections with \texttt{part:} in the \texttt{chapters:} list, e.g. \texttt{part: "Basics"} followed by its own nested \texttt{chapters:} list.
\item Add an \texttt{appendices:} list at the book level --- auto-numbered ``Appendix A'', ``Appendix B'', \ldots
\item Cross-reference any chapter from anywhere in the book: give a heading an id with \texttt{\{\#sec-intro\}}, then link to it with \texttt{@sec-intro}.
\end{itemize}
\end{spotlight}
```
